question: Which country hosted the 17th BRICS Summit in July 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Brazil (Rio de Janeiro)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 17th **BRICS Summit** was hosted by **Brazil** in its famous city of **Rio de Janeiro** in **July 2025**.
 
• BRICS is an acronym for an association of five major economies: **Brazil, Russia, India, China,** and **South Africa**.
 
• Brazil has previously hosted other BRICS summits, highlighting its active participation in the bloc's economic and political discussions.
 
• The summit in Rio de Janeiro focused on enhancing economic cooperation, sustainable development, and addressing global challenges like **climate change** and **geopolitical stability**.
 
• Rio de Janeiro is renowned for its **natural beauty** and iconic landmarks such as **Christ the Redeemer**, making it a fitting venue for an international summit.
 
• Brazil's hosting of the summit reflects its commitment to strengthening diplomatic ties within the BRICS framework and addressing critical global issues.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Russia**__

 __
 
• **Russia** is one of the founding members of BRICS and has hosted multiple BRICS summits in the past, including the 7th BRICS Summit in **Ufa** in **2015**.
 
• It plays a significant role in BRICS discussions, particularly in areas like **energy** and **geopolitical security**.
 
 
 
• **India**__
 __
 
• **India** is another founding member of BRICS and has hosted summits like the 8th BRICS Summit in **Goa** in **2016**.
 
• India focuses on issues such as **technology**, **innovation**, and **inclusive development** within the BRICS framework.
 
 
 
• **South Africa**__
 
 
• **South Africa** joined BRICS in **2010**, representing the continent of **Africa**.
 
• South Africa hosted the 15th BRICS Summit in **Durban** in **2023**, emphasizing **African development** and global cooperation.
